title: One Style Fits All? Cultural Values Embedded in Conversational AI via a People-Pleasing Lens
abstract: arXiv:2611.32939v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Conversational AI systems trained on large-scale web corpora inevitably encode the cultural values and interactional norms embedded in their training data, yet our understanding of how deployed LLMs reflect or reinforce culture-specific social expectations remains limited. This study examined how supportive versus challenging chatbot interaction styles shape user experience and continuance intention, and whether people-pleasing tendency (PPT) moderates these effects across cultures. Taiwanese (N = 49) and Korean (N = 52) participants completed a collaborative tourism-planning task. translated_title: 一种风格适用于所有人？从讨好倾向视角审视对话式AI中嵌入的文化价值观
translated_abstract: 基于大规模网络语料训练的对话式AI系统不可避免地编码了其训练数据中蕴含的文化价值观与互动规范，然而我们对已部署的大语言模型如何反映或强化特定文化的社会期望的理解仍然有限。本研究考察了支持型与挑战型聊天机器人交互风格如何塑造用户体验与持续使用意愿，以及取悦倾向是否在不同文化间调节这些效应。来自台湾（N = 49）和韩国（N = 52）的参与者完成了一项协作式旅游规划任务。结果表明：（1）支持型聊天机器人在持续使用意愿、满意度和信任方面始终表现更佳；（2）取悦倾向并未调节这些效应；（3）文化差异仅出现在感知威胁层面，即在台湾样本中较高的取悦倾向与更高的基线威胁感相关，而在韩国样本中则不然。这些发现揭示了……（原文摘要到此截断）
tldr: 研究发现，无论在台湾还是韩国，支持型聊天机器人风格都能稳定提升用户的持续使用意愿、满意度和信任，而取悦倾向并不调节这些效应，仅在感知威胁上存在文化差异。
en_tdlr: Across Taiwanese and Korean samples, a supportive chatbot style consistently increased continuance intention, satisfaction, and trust, with people-pleasing tendency showing no moderating effect—except for a cultural difference in perceived threat.
